purpose: Idelalisib is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including a type of leukemia called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and some types of lymphoma. It is usually used in patients whose cancer has come back or has not responded well to other treatments. It is often given in combination with another medicine called rituximab.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a specific protein called PI3K-delta that helps them grow and survive. Idelalisib works by blocking this protein, which cuts off the signal that tells cancer cells to keep growing. Think of it like turning off a switch that the cancer cells need to stay alive.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea or loose stools, nausea, tiredness, fever, chills, rash, cough, shortness of breath, stomach pain, and low blood cell counts (which can make you more prone to infections or bleeding).
warnings: This medicine can cause serious and sometimes life-threatening problems including severe diarrhea, liver damage, serious lung inflammation, intestinal tears, and severe skin reactions. It also raises your risk of serious infections. You will need regular blood tests to monitor your liver and blood counts. Tell your doctor right away if you develop diarrhea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, trouble breathing, or a severe rash. Do not use if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg taken by mouth twice a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. Do not crush or chew the tablets. Your doctor may lower your dose or have you stop temporarily if you develop certain side effects.
